title: Planets align over La Silla
caption: Jupiter, Venus and Mercury aligned over La Silla Observatory at sunset
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The Sun sets over ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile, leaving a fiery orange glow along the horizon. Just left of centre, three planets line up over the telescopes. According to the source, Jupiter is at the bottom left, almost lost in the sunset, Venus is in the middle and Mercury is at the top right.

David Jones took the picture in June 2013, while observing for five nights with the 3.6-metre New Technology Telescope. He was fortunate to have observing time at just the right moment. The close grouping lasted only a week or so, and he noted that the next such event would come in 2026.

Such alignments come around only once every several years. When three or more celestial objects line up in the sky it is called a syzygy. La Silla sits on the edge of the Atacama Desert in one of the driest places on Earth, where the steady air gives very clear views.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph by David Jones, blended from two exposures of different lengths. The source gives no other camera or colour details.
understand.eye: The eye adjusts as it looks around a scene, while this picture blends two exposures of different lengths to show the observing site in detail.
